family.name: one-factor Gaussian-copula conditional-independence closure 1FGC-8
family.dependence_state: one common latent Gaussian factor plus scalar marginals

novelty.substantive_continuation: 1FGC can represent R215's perfect correlated/anti-correlated 2D witnesses with loadings (1,1) and (1,-1), so it genuinely adds shared dependence rather than adding marginal frequencies.

primary_literature.title: Factor copula models for multivariate data
primary_literature.claim_used: conditional-independence copula models with latent factors; O(d) dependence parameterization; factor-structured Gaussian copula as a special case

primary_literature.author: Andre Nataf
primary_literature.title: Determination des distributions de probabilites dont les marges sont donnees
primary_literature.claim_used: normal-copula style construction separating prescribed marginals from dependence

exact_small.parity_law: uniform on the eight Rademacher states with X1*X2*X3*X4=+1
exact_small.gaussian_one_factor_constraint: Corr(sign Zi, sign Zj)=2/pi*asin(lambda_i*lambda_j); zero pair correlations imply lambda_i*lambda_j=0 for every i!=j, hence at most one loading is nonzero and the modeled observed joint law is independent

terminal_reason: A single Gaussian latent factor is not an information-complete dependence carrier. The exact even-parity law has the same univariate marginals and all pair laws as independence, forcing the one-factor Gaussian-copula state to the independent representation, while the next dense ReLU observable differs by 1/4.
boundary: This closes only one-factor Gaussian-copula conditional-independence closure. Multi-factor copulas, vines, or explicit higher-order dependence carriers are different families and are not R219 rescue.
